bib.title: Cut Your Losses in Large-Vocabulary Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; figure curve data not readable from text.

question: How can the cross-entropy loss layer of large-vocabulary LLMs be computed without materializing the N x |V| logit matrix in GPU memory, without losing speed or convergence?
hypothesis: Because softmax is extremely sparse, blocks of the gradient below bf16 precision can be skipped, so a fused kernel computing logits in SRAM gives negligible memory with no speed or convergence cost.
contributions: Cut Cross-Entropy (CCE): loss decomposed into an indexed matmul plus a linear-log-sum-exp, computed blockwise in SRAM by custom Triton kernels
Gradient filtering of softmax blocks below 2^-12 and vocabulary sorting by average logit
Benchmarks against Baseline, torch.compile, Torch Tune and Liger Kernels, plus fine-tuning and pretraining convergence checks

method.summary: Rewrites cross-entropy as the correct-token logit (indexed matmul fused in one kernel) minus a log-sum-exp over the vocabulary computed blockwise with a spin-lock atomic log-add-exp; backward recomputes logits in SRAM and skips blocks whose softmax values are all below eps=2^-12, with vocabulary reordered by average logit to densify blocks. Implemented in Triton.
method.task: memory-efficient cross-entropy loss and gradient for LLM training

datasets.name: Alpaca
datasets.preprocessing: inputs/labels for kernel benchmarks and fine-tuning; ignored tokens removable (Appendix B)

training.objective: next-token cross-entropy (fine-tuning on Alpaca; pretraining on Open WebText), CCE vs torch.compile control
training.steps: loss curves plotted to ~700 gradient steps for fine-tuning (read from Fig 4 axes)
training.precision: bf16 (gradient accumulated in global memory in final float type); Kahan summation in CCE-Kahan
training.hardware: A100-SXM4 80GB for kernel benchmarks; training hardware not stated
training.wall_clock: Mistral NeMo: CCE-Kahan-FullC with doubled batch size saves 2 hours (16%) vs torch.compile

other.note: The paper states no optimizer, learning rate, batch size or sequence length for the convergence experiments; Fig 1 assumes AdamW mixed-precision 16-bit, 16x80GB FSDP with activation checkpointing.

inference.samples: 5 seeds averaged for all timings and curves

other.synchronisation: spin-lock on atomic in global memory (Triton)

limits: Implemented in Triton; control flow (lock, filter) is block-level only, authors expect CUDA to be faster.
Advantage in time shrinks as |V|/D falls (Phi 3.5 Mini 50% slower than torch.compile); parallelism is B x |V| so large D adds work not parallelism.
Gradient filtering on gradC starves rare tokens; pretraining needs the slower CCE-Kahan-FullC, which is roughly 2x+ slower than torch.compile in kernel time.
Convergence experiments omit optimizer, learning rate, batch size, sequence length, step count and hardware; confidence from 5 seeds with curves only.
Only memory and time of the loss layer and curves were tested; no downstream task evaluation.
Max-batch-size claim uses an analytic memory model (float32 logits only, 75 GB usable), which the authors say likely undercounts.
